A 34-year-old pregnant woman at 33 weeks gestation presents to the emergency department with a
persistent headache that differs from her usual migraines and is accompanied by double vision. She
reports chills and multiple episodes of vomiting. Her vital signs include a temperature of 98.3°F
(36.8°C), blood pressure of 156/92 mmHg, pulse of 106/min, respirations of 25/min, and oxygen
saturation of 99% on room air. On physical examination, she appears uncomfortable. A cranial nerve
examination reveals an inability to abduct her left eye, and her gait is mildly ataxic. What is the most
appropriate next step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A) MRI brain with gadolinium (B)
Urgent neurology consultation (C) Serial neurological examinations (D) Immediate magnesium sulfate
administration (E) Lumbar puncture (F) Acetaminophen and bed rest (G) CT head without contrast (H)
MR venogram of the brain (I) Empiric antibiotic therapy (J) CT angiogram of the head
